_readme: Reputation copy (Saga), v2, pass-2 voice. Aligned to docs/design/reputation-v0.1.md v0.1.2 and councils-v0.1.md at repo commit 0e93339. Finalises the §7 display ladder (L3 titles exact; L4/L5 adopted as defined; L1–L2 unchanged from v1), the §7.4 epithets (exact, including challenge_won), directory and meeting-card strings (E9), stranger-greeting variants (E1, L2+ only), and gossip for title gained, title lost ('once called…'), and pole flip. Tundra's settled rulings: Q3 plain sum; Q4 retreats count only when an ally is left behind; Q5 land taken or lost feeds only the land_taker epithet; councils Honour affects belief, not who may speak. Anna (2026-11-10) signed off the four specs: reputation never fades; secrets coming out are reputation moments (see secrets); a pride holds 3 to 6 regions; a grudge-holder lies 1 time in 4; councils are once a season plus emergencies; only pride leaders attend. Selection, tokens and bans are unchanged from v1. Does not invent mechanics, cats, or lore, and does not invent epithets beyond §7.4.

_source.hooks: §7–§9, E1, E2, E9; councils-v0.1 §5.2 settles E4/Q6

_tokens.name: The run name of the cat the line is about (world-gen §3). On directory, meeting-card, epithet and gossip lines, that is the subject cat. On greeting lines, that is the player.
_tokens.sourceName: The cat who told the player the gossip (same token as map-danger-gossip-v1). Used on gossip lines.
_tokens.teller: Alias for the gossip teller, whitelisted and not used in the lines. Bind this to the same cat as {sourceName} if an older hook expected it.
_tokens.prideName: The pride the line is about. On pride_words and the My Pride unknown line, that is the pride being described. On challenge_won, that is the pride's name as stored on the feat fact at the time of the win, including a founded pride.
_tokens.subjectName: the subject cat on secret-reveal and gossip lines; same binding as {name} in those lines

_schema.when: First match wins; the last entry in a list has no when and is the default. Matches if every key present is true. axis is mercy, courage or honour. pole is positive or negative (signed, as in the spec). level is the exact known level L2, L3, L4 or L5 (not a minimum; greetings are E1 L2+ only). sociability, aggression, boldness and loyalty are the teller's or greeter's trait band (high / low; baseline is the unbanded default). Trait hooks appear only where E1 or E2 states a like or dislike. Trait keys in this bank are listed in the order sociability, aggression, boldness, loyalty, so an NPC who matches two high traits takes the earlier hook. prideKnown is true only when {prideName} can be filled on a challenge_won line (the observer knows the place of that win).
_schema.words: Lookup by axis, pole, level (L1–L5). L1–L2 are words only. L3 is the title, exact from §7. L4/L5 are the §7 strings, adopted as defined. Directory word lines use this table for every known axis at L1 or higher. The meeting card shows one title: the highest-level axis (ties go Courage, then Mercy, then Honour; see _rules). At L3+ the title line is this table's string for that axis. At L4+ the meeting card prefers this L4/L5 string, then an epithet, then an L3 title (priority is an engine rule).
_schema.pride_words: The same ladder with {prideName} as the subject, per §8.1. L3 uses '{prideName} the Merciful' (and '{prideName} Oathbreaker', no 'the'), which the spec does not spell out; see _questions.
_schema.epithets: Exact §7.4 strings, keyed by featId. challenge_won is a first-when-wins list: the {prideName} form when prideKnown is true, then a general no-place default with no when (see _rules).
_schema.directory: E9 field label and the unknown string, plus the same unknown for a meeting card with nothing known. Word lines and the title line are looked up from words (and pride_words for a pride).
_schema.my_pride: §8.3 header hook: one Reputation line in words. The known line is pride_words for the founded pride's highest axis. unknown is an adaptation of E9, because the spec does not give a pride unknown string; see _questions.
_schema.greetings: NPC speech to the player at a stranger first-meeting (E1). Selected by the player's highest known axis at L2+, with trait bands from E1/E2. Ties use the settled §7.3 order (Courage, then Mercy, then Honour; see _rules). The last entry is the default when nothing is known.
_schema.gossip: title_gained, title_lost and pole_flip. Each is a first-when-wins list, per axis and pole, with teller sociability high, then low, then unbanded, then a final default. title_lost uses 'once called…'. pole.pole is the pole the talk has turned TO, and the lines do not award the opposite title.
_schema.secrets: Anna (2026-11-10): when a secret comes out it becomes a reputation moment, never seeded as known (§9.1). Lookup is by secret id (ln01_silence, ln04_saved_cub, hc02_fallen_cub). slot is the subject cat. learned is the first-hand Lore Book / moment line. gossip, widely_told, confirmed, false_variant and debunked follow the Lore Book rumour pattern. {name} and {subjectName} are the subject cat. Role names are never used.

_rules.tie_order: When two or more known axes are at the same level, titles (meeting card, §7.3) and stranger greetings (E1) both use Courage, then Mercy, then Honour. Settled by Tundra and Flint. Tundra: Courage is the axis a stranger most likely heard of. Titles and greetings share this order. This is an engine selection rule, not copy; the bank does not encode the tie.
_rules.challenge_won: Tundra, PROPOSED DEFAULT. The feat fact stores the pride's name as it was at the time of the win; {prideName} binds to that stored name. The player's own (founded) pride counts like any other pride, so it uses the same {prideName} form. If the place is unknown to the observer, use the last entry, the general no-place line. If the observer knows several wins, show the most recent one they know (engine selection, not copy). The earlier by-pride nicknames (Crag-Taker / Field-Taker / Mist-Taker) are replaced by this form.

_gaps: No L1 greeting hook: E1 is L2+ only. An L1-only player uses the default stranger greeting.

No greeting variants for trait bands E1/E2 do not mention (low sociability, low boldness, low loyalty, and low aggression except vs Cruel). High aggression vs Cruel is 0 (doesn't mind) and is not banded.
Ambient deed templates rep.ambient.{axis}.{pole}.{class} (§9.2) are not in this bank.

E4 Faithless L3+ council distrust lines, E5 Cruel L3+ danger text, and E7 trespass patrol variants are text-only hooks not in this bank. Councils-v0.1 §5.2 now settles E4: Honour changes how likely a leader is to be believed, not who may speak. The distrust, danger and patrol lines still need a later copy pass.
_questions: Flint: E1 greetings are L2+ only. This bank has no L1 greeting. Confirm an L1-only known axis uses the default (nothing known) greeting, not a special L1 line.
Flint: E1 is stranger first-meetings (slice.meeting.*, the first stored pair value, cats-come-to-you). Confirm these lines do not replace repeat-meeting greetings.
Flint: when.level on greetings is the exact known level (L2, L3, L4 or L5), not a minimum. Confirm you pass the exact level of the single highest known axis (ties: Courage, then Mercy, then Honour).

Flint: walk each list in order (first when match wins). Trait hooks are listed sociability, then aggression, then boldness, then loyalty, so an NPC who is high in two matching traits takes the earlier hook.

Flint: {name} on greeting lines is the player's run name (reputation §7.1). On directory, epithet and gossip lines, {name} is the subject cat. {sourceName} is the gossip teller. {teller} is whitelisted and unused; bind it to the same cat if an older hook expected it.

Flint / Tundra: pride_words follow §8.1. The L3 pride title form is still not specified. This bank keeps '{prideName} the Merciful' and '{prideName} Oathbreaker' (no 'the') as the closest reading of 'the same words'. Confirm or supply a pride title form.

Flint / Tundra: §8.3 says My Pride's summary header gets one Reputation line in words. This bank provides my_pride.unknown ('Nothing said of {prideName} yet') as an adaptation of E9, and says the known line is pride_words for the highest axis. Confirm the unknown string and that the header uses pride_words.

Flint: meeting-card priority (an L4+ axis title, then an epithet, then an L3 title) is an engine rule. L4/L5 title strings in §7 do not include {name} ('Renowned for mercy'). Confirm they are shown as-is, or say if {name} should be prefixed.
Flint: the directory field label is 'Reputation' per E9. That word is otherwise banned in player-facing prose; it is stored here as a UI label only.

Flint: secrets (ln01_silence, ln04_saved_cub, hc02_fallen_cub) are in the secrets bank. Anna ruled they become reputation moments when they come out, and they are never seeded as known (§9.1). Confirm the hook: first-when-wins is not used here; look up by secret id. {name} is the subject cat. Role names (the lore names for these slots) must not appear on screen.
Flint: M6, should a clean steal stay private (the owner is currently in participants on success)? This is reputation Q8, still open.
Saga note for Flint: title-lost lines use the number word 'once' only inside the required phrase 'once called' (§7.3). The validator allows that phrase and no other 'once'.

_resolved: Q3: a plain sum, with no extra weight for acting against type (Tundra, 2026-11-10).
Q4: a retreat counts only when you leave an ally behind (Tundra, 2026-11-10).
Q5: land taken or lost counts toward no axis and only feeds the land_taker epithet (Tundra, 2026-11-10).
Q6 / councils: Honour affects whether leaders believe you, not who gets to speak (councils-v0.1 §5.2).
Anna (2026-11-10), reputation: it never fades. It sticks for life. No copy says a name or deed is fading or forgotten. Titles may still be lost through opposing deeds (§7.3).
Anna (2026-11-10), Q9: secrets coming out become reputation moments. Copy is in secrets (ln01 silence, ln04 saved cub, hc02 fallen cub), never seeded as known (§9.1).
Anna (2026-11-10), map: a pride holds 3 to 6 regions. Counts stay out of player-facing prose.
Anna (2026-11-10), lore-book §3.3: a cat with a grudge lies about 1 time in 4. False variants stay behind the crossed-out mechanism; the rate is never shown.
Anna (2026-11-10), councils: a council happens once a season, plus an early one when a feud boils over.
Anna (2026-11-10), councils: only pride leaders attend. Loners cannot ask to come, and no copy offers that.
